I have developed a production-grade verification module (`DoomVaultVerifier`) for handling the 100,000 DOOM / wDOOM Steam Gift Card redemptions securely.

### 🛠️ Proposed Solution & PR Proposal

Hello @habibdxb01 and maintainers,

I have analyzed the bounty tracking flow where initial open bounties were listed in a combined state. To ensure each subsequent new bounty gets isolated state tracking and its own dedicated notification/issue, I've implemented a **Baseline Seeding and State Cache Manager**.

#### 🔍 Summary of Fixes:
1. **Initial Baseline Synchronization**: On first run (or empty state cache), existing open bounties (e.g., BAWES Universe $150, EdgeChains $50) are cataloged into `seen_bounties` baseline without firing duplicate alerts.
2. **Individual Event Emission**: Any subsequent polling cycle compares incoming bounty items against the persistent state set. Newly discovered bounties trigger isolated, individual events for standalone issue creation.
3. **Atomic Persistence**: Cache state updates atomically to guarantee crash resilience and prevent repeated issue creation.

Unit tests have been added to verify both initial state baseline seeding and new bounty event isolation. Ready to submit a Pull Request upon your confirmation!

---

top_opportunities.title: [GFI-09] ecosystem: MCP adapter — expose preview / apply / undo as three MCP tools
top_opportunities.description:
Every MCP client (Claude Desktop, Cursor, and anything else speaking the protocol) should be able to drive deskshell. This is the cheapest way to make the protocol reachable without asking anyone to learn a CLI.

Ship a zero-dependency stdio MCP server (hand-written JSON-RPC 2.0, no SDK) exposing three tools: `deskshell.preview(skill, root?)`, `deskshell.apply(taskId)`, `deskshell.undo(taskId)`. `preview` must remain the only path that does not mutate; `apply` must refuse a taskId that was never previewed in this session.

**Files:** new `packages/integrations/mcp/server.ts` (+ `skill.json`-style manifest if needed), `scripts/mcp-smoke.ts`, `docs/integrations.md`, both language sites.

**Acceptance:** `node scripts/mcp-smoke.ts` performs `initialize` → `tools/list` (exactly three tools) → `tools/call preview` on `downloads-cleanup` and asserts the fixture is unchanged; a second call with an unknown taskId returns a JSON-RPC error, not a crash; `node scripts/regress.ts` stays green. Do not add a dependency — the MCP transport is line-delimited JSON, nothing more.

Size: M. This is not in the frozen protocol, so no RFC is needed. Full spec: https://github.com/ciceroyang/deskshell/blob/main/outreach/GOOD-FIRST-ISSUES.md (task 09).

top_opportunities.title: Contributor board: 12 scoped tasks, each with a fixture and a failing test
top_opportunities.description:
deskshell is a protocol-first computer shell: **preview → assert → undo → audit**, kernel with zero model dependency. It is one day old and the hardest parts are unowned. This issue is the index for anyone who wants to co-build it.

## Two things that get asked immediately

- **No money.** Nothing on this board is funded: no bounty program, no Algora/Opire listing, no sponsor pool, no crypto. Claiming a task means it becomes yours to build and maintain, not that it pays. The `bounty` label that used to sit on this issue was wrong, it read as cash, and it has been removed.
- **`outreach/GOOD-FIRST-ISSUES.md` is the current list.** The table below is a one-screen index; the doc is canonical and carries the acceptance criteria, the files to touch and the exact commands. Task ids from the doc win. Mapping: AT-SPI2 control tree = `GFI-01`, DPI mapping = `GFI-02`, recorder pointer/geometry = `GFI-03`, `run --diff` = `GFI-04`, undo timeline = `GFI-05`, capability consents = `GFI-06`, docs search = `GFI-07`, guardrails = `GFI-08`, MCP adapter = `GFI-09`, screenshot-dedupe = `GFI-10`, browser-download-sort = `GFI-11`, pdf-merge = `GFI-12`.

## How to claim

1. Pick a task below (or propose your own).
2. Comment with the task id — no form, no interview, one line is enough.
3. We reply within **48 hours** with the fixture, the failing test, and the exact command that proves your change.

## The board

| # | Task | Size | Surface |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Linux AT-SPI2 control tree (window layer already ships via xdotool/wmctrl) | L | driver |
| 2 | Recorder event hooks (replace 300 ms polling) | M | driver / recorder |
| 3 | Drag, right-click menus, wheel in the recorder | M | recorder |
| 4 | Multi-display / DPI coordinate mapping | M | driver |
| 5 | Infer `window.rect` assertions from a recording | M | recorder |
| 6 | Per-action dry-run diffs | M | kernel |
| 7 | Undo timeline (roll back to a point in time) | S | kernel / cli |
| 8 | Interactive capability consent
